title: PRODUCT-BUG fix: a guest replica's equal-revision cache no longer stands over a forced server refresh

buildIdentity.commitSubject: fix(campaign): never let a guest replica's equal-revision cache stand over a server refresh
buildIdentity.originMainDriftDuringSession: origin/main advanced from the 95042d919 base to 5fac5a58c while this work was in flight (a concurrent merge by another session). The commit itself is unaffected: git diff --stat 95042d919..8a2975c81 is exactly the 4 files below. A rebase onto the newer head has NOT been performed here.

rootCause: src/stores/campaign/useCampaignPersistenceStore.ts runLoad computed cacheStands from evaluateCampaignCache (src/lib/campaign/persistence/campaignCacheKey.ts) alone, which compares only (instanceId, revision). For a source client that pair implies equal content, because only its own PUT moves the revision. For a GUEST the copy is a replica mutated by host broadcast and local session state, so it can diverge in content at a still revision; cacheStands was therefore true, loadedCampaign stayed the stale local copy and writeLiveCampaign was skipped, silently undoing the forced guest refresh at src/pages-modules/gameplay/campaigns/campaignPageShell.tsx:144-146 (guestNeedsServerRefresh, #1022).

fix.productionChange: src/stores/campaign/useCampaignPersistenceStore.ts — cacheStands additionally requires liveCampaign.coopSession?.mode !== 'guest' (9 added / 1 removed lines, of which 6 are the explanatory comment).
fix.unchangedByDesign: Host and single-player paths: a source client's copy IS what the server record was written from, so the keyed-cache policy is untouched for them.
fix.replacementBranchAlreadyCorrect: preserveGuestCoopSession (:252-266) keeps the guest coopSession across the whole-record replacement, so the co-op surfaces survive the refresh — verified by an assertion in the new test rows, not assumed.

specCarveOut.rationale: The existing scenario 'Stale cache is refreshed, not trusted' scopes staleness to revision N < head M only, so a guest whose content diverged at EQUAL revision fell through it. The carve-out narrows when a cache may stand rather than weakening the keyed-cache policy for source clients.
